reasoning: The theoretical claim the proposal builds on (a proxy is unhackable only if it captures the full true reward; no non-trivial unhackable proxies exist) is rigorously established by Skalse et al. 2022 (NeurIPS), and the empirical relationship between proxy misspecification severity and true-reward degradation is directly studied by Pan et al. 2022 (ICLR, "Effects of Reward Misspecification"), which maps reward hacking as a function of misspecification type and agent capability and even finds phase transitions. However, the specific proposed contribution — incrementally adding individual known true-reward *components* to a proxy and plotting residual optimal-policy regret (residual hackability) against the *fraction of components captured*, computed via exhaustive policy enumeration in small deterministic gridworlds — does not appear to have been published as such. Pan et al. vary optimization pressure/capability with trained RL agents rather than enumerate policies over a component-coverage axis, so the specific "residual-hackability-vs-fraction-captured curve" angle is a genuine, if narrow, gap on top of a well-explored problem.

evidence.title: Defining and Characterizing Reward Hacking (Skalse et al.)
evidence.summary: Theoretical anchor for the proposal: proves no non-trivial proxy reward is unhackable, and that a proxy is unhackable only if it effectively captures the full true reward (over all stochastic policies, two rewards are unhackable only if one is constant). Establishes the 'unhackability limit' the proposal references but provides no empirical residual-hackability curve.

evidence.title: The Effects of Reward Misspecification: Mapping and Mitigating Misaligned Models (Pan et al.)
evidence.summary: Closest empirical work: constructs RL environments with misspecified proxy rewards (taxonomized as misweighting, incorrect ontology, incorrect scope) and measures how true reward degrades as a function of agent capability, finding phase transitions where true reward sharply drops. Studies proxy fidelity vs hacking severity empirically but via trained agents and capability axes, not enumeration over fraction-of-components-captured.

evidence.title: Correlated Proxies: A New Definition and Improved Mitigation for Reward Hacking (Laidlaw et al.)
evidence.summary: Provides a correlation-based definition of reward hacking and mitigation; characterizes the proxy-true reward relationship and shows hacking even at high correlation. Adjacent to the proposal but frames the proxy-true gap via correlation/regularization rather than a monotone component-coverage curve computed by full policy enumeration.

evidence.title: Defining and Characterising Reward Hacking (community discussion)
evidence.summary: Community summary reiterating that ensuring a proxy is unhackable requires capturing all details of true preferences, and that the residual gap always leaves room for exploitation — confirming the framing is well-understood in the safety community but not operationalized as the proposed fraction-captured empirical curve.
